investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-30T12:31–12:32Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api gateway could not reach the swarm backend at the AWS ELB endpoint used for POST /v1/agents. Because the failure occurs before any agent is provisioned, all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and no contract assertions can be evaluated.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend, reachable through an AWS ELB in us-east-2 at the /v1/agents endpoint, was unreachable from the production-api gateway at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". This upstream connectivity failure caused every remote-agents check to abort before producing any evidence, making this an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the swarm gateway / ELB target, not a defect in the eval runner or contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

This is an isolated eval failure scoped to the snapshot freshness assertion; all sibling public-website checks passed, and there is no evidence of a user-facing outage.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing status.json to the GitHub Pages endpoint has not run successfully in at least 685 minutes (approximately 11.4 hours). The contract requires snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300 (5 hours). The snapshot itself is structurally valid and carries real feature data (featureCount=19, unknownFeatureCount=0, hasNonUnknownFeatureData=true, hasLiveSource=true), so the failure is exclusively a staleness violation, not a data-quality or schema problem. The upstream cause — why the workflow has not produced a fresh snapshot — is uncertain from the supplied evidence alone; it could be a missed schedule trigger, a workflow failure, a GitHub Actions quota or permissions issue, or a publishing step failure.
